title: Formal Cause Connectors in Economic Analysis

sections.content:
You know *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6. In economic columns and reports, writers choose among four formal connectors depending on whether they name a noun phrase or a full clause, and whether the cause is a trigger, a known premise or a direct chain.

*Debido a*, *a raíz de* and *como consecuencia de* take a noun phrase or an infinitive. *Debido a* gives a neutral cause; *a raíz de* points to a specific event that triggered a change; *como consecuencia de* stresses the resulting effect. *Dado que* takes a conjugated verb in the indicative and introduces a fact the reader already accepts as the premise of the argument.

sections.title: Formal cause connectors
rows: triggering event (following / as a result of)
como consecuencia de + noun phrase / infinitive
cause framed through its effect (as a consequence of)

items.spanish: El consumo cayó debido al encarecimiento del crédito.
items.english: Consumption fell because of the rising cost of credit.

items.spanish: A raíz de la crisis en la cadena de suministro, varios productos se encarecieron.
items.english: Following the crisis in the supply chain, several products became more expensive.

items.spanish: Como consecuencia de la inflación, las familias perdieron poder adquisitivo.
items.english: As a consequence of inflation, households lost purchasing power.

items.spanish: Dado que las tasas de interés siguen altas, el crédito resulta más caro.
items.english: Given that interest rates remain high, credit is more expensive.

sections.content: Watch the complement: *debido a*, *a raíz de* and *como consecuencia de* take a noun, never a bare conjugated verb (*debido a que* is needed before a clause). Conversely, *dado que* requires a conjugated verb in the indicative, never a bare noun or the subjunctive. Remember the contraction *a + el = al* (*debido al encarecimiento*).
